there is no convincing evidence that the QPO phenomenon is related to the orbital or rotational motion of the compact object in the system, or that it is related to any other periodicity of the compact object.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that the epicyclic motion of a perturbed accretion disk can produce resonant oscillations at the epicyclical frequencies and that the strongest response is at the half-frequency difference between the two epicyclic motions.

the observed QPO frequencies in accreting neutron star and black hole systems are not the epicyclic oscillations of an orbiting fluid element, but rather the forced oscillations of the accretion disk itself.

we have shown that a resonant response can occur between two epicyclic oscillations in a perturbed torus and the response occurs when the difference in frequency between the two oscillations equals the forcing frequency.
